column1: # The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB. The NPDM declares 48 MB of system resource.
# 8 GB alias region stops OptimizeChangeBanc thread freeze in Kokiri Forest.
# Android: the host's frame limiter's default is 60 fps, the game's own top rate (the launcher's Frame rate cap, 60 / 45 / 40 / 30 / 20, and DM_FPS_LIMIT override it). Until
# 2026-11-11 it was 30: Link's house ran 37-38 fps from cool and 27-32 once hot, the phone 23 C warmer over a run; at 30 every frame is 33.3 ms and it warms 12 C (README.md
# "Profile"). The maintainer chose the game's own rate as the start; 30 is one tap away in the in-game panel
# Android: two pixel shaders whose draws later drawing covers (a sky-like layer: 6 draws of the first and 2 of the second cost 34 of 77 ms of GPU time at Link's house on an
# Adreno 740 with Turnip). The launcher's Game settings offer "Speedhack: Turn off hidden layers (experimental)" for them (DM_VK_SKIP_FS), off by default: judged by eye in
# Kokiri Forest and Link's house only
# The frame step (patches.py) in whole vsyncs decided by the host, also with no limit (the launcher's 60): left to the game's own controller, the game kept interval 1 at 25 fps on the
# phone (0.4 of real time; its controller's frame costs, framework +0x148 / +0x150, said 60 fits). The limit above caps the step (hle_fpslock.c dm_fps_step_fold): 30 fps = 2 vsyncs a frame
# The window crop the scene is upscaled into follows the operation mode and the Switch 2 graphics scale, not a window getter (README, Render size): the display state
# (main+0x6502e0) takes the scale from oe::GetCurrentGraphicsScale (main+0xe376d8) and picks the crop from a size table (main+0x112c5e0, as Mario Kart World):
# handheld scale 0 or 1 1920x1080, scale 2 1280x720 where the handheld parameters allow it; console scale 1 2560x1440 (at most: the crop is also capped by the mode's
# base size times the scale's factor, 2048x1152 on Mario Kart World). The Android launcher's Game resolution sets these. Phone 1440p and Original are console scale 1,
# the console's own docked picture (console mode: the game reports a docked controller and runs its scale-1-only passes). 540p and 480p have no row: no mode and scale
# goes below 1280x720, so they take the smallest row, 1280x720 (Profile.resolutionEnv)
# agl wraps its clears in render conditions on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders; the same library here
